Industrial Securities · 兴业 SMT2022–23In-house · securities software

Make a securities interface reusable.

At Wuhan Youpin Chuding Technology, I worked with colleagues to break down business modules, then designed and maintained the relevant Figma components and specifications.

Problem
In securities software, controls that look the same can carry very different business consequences. Components split by appearance alone get reused in the wrong places.
Key decisions
I set component boundaries by business meaning rather than appearance, and defined four states for the positions table — default, selected, hover and no data — so that feedback changes while position and reading order stay put.
Outcome
Part of the redesign of Industrial Securities’ SMT 5.0 trading system, which was built and launched; the components were reused across projects and in day and night themes.

01 · The challenge

A table carries a task, not just data.

A securities tool brings accounts, markets, positions, values and actions into a dense working surface. Visually similar controls can have very different consequences, so component boundaries cannot be based on appearance alone.

The aim was to reduce repeated interface construction while preserving business meaning. I researched component-library methods and business-unit decomposition with colleagues, then developed the relevant structures into components and guidelines.

Context

Which account?

Account and market context determine how the data should be understood.

State

What is happening?

Default, selected, hover and no-data states need distinct feedback.

Action

What can I do?

Each action belongs to a task and must retain its business meaning.

02 · Decomposition

Use business meaning to decide what can be shared.

For account positions, the table, account context and controls can become reusable units while keeping their relationships explicit. A shared structure only works when its meaning and behaviour match.

My responsibility included the relevant component design, usage specifications and ongoing maintenance. Where tasks have different rules, preserving those differences matters more than forcing consistency.

Tobie’s note

A component boundary is also a product-design decision.

03 · States

Let state change without moving the reading structure.

The source “Table / Account Positions” component includes default, selected, hover and no-data variants. Feedback needs to explain what changed while keeping information position and reading order stable.

The specification therefore addresses both appearance and behaviour across situations. Consistent state definitions also give maintenance work a shared reference.

04 · Specifications & maintenance

Share the structure; preserve the meaning of the action.

Buy, sell, confirm, cancel and input controls have related structures, but are not the same action. I maintained components and specifications to give repeated modules a consistent foundation while preserving these distinctions.

The components supported cross-project reuse and day/night theme adaptation.

05 · Screens

From components to full screens.

Beyond the components, I designed full screens for the system: the asset home, quick order, basket order and grid strategy. Each screen is assembled from the same set of components — the account selector, order panel, order book and positions table look the same and sit in the same place from one screen to the next.

06 · Age-friendly design

Turning “age-friendly” into rules a team can build from.

From April to June 2022 I designed a “Care mode” proposal for Daton Securities’ trading app: I broke the client’s age-friendly upgrade requirement down into interaction rules for the trading flow, applied them screen by screen, and delivered a complete prototype proposal.

Larger type. Core text and action buttons are scaled to 1.25×; no text on a screen is smaller than 18pt.

Bigger tap targets. Tap areas of main components are larger than 60×60pt on the home screen and 44×44pt elsewhere.

Words instead of icons. Icons and abbreviations on the home screen become full text labels; the bottom tabs become large text.

Re-lay out after enlarging. With larger type and buttons, screens move to a single column and the order book moves below the form. Inputs that can be merged are merged: enter a stock code and the system picks the market.

No novel interactions. Currency switching changes from a swipe to a text button plus a bottom sheet; tapping a holding also opens a bottom sheet.

Secondary features step back. Features are grouped by information type, frequency of use and importance: frequent ones get large tiles and high-contrast blocks, and those older users rarely need are toned down.

The company adopted the proposal as its standard age-friendly pitch for bids, and it was reused in a later bid for Shengang Securities. The prototype was also broken down into components the team could reuse.

07 · Outcome & reflection

A reusable design foundation starts with clear boundaries.

The components and guidelines went into the redesign of Industrial Securities’ SMT 5.0 trading system, which was built and launched. I delivered the Figma components, usage guidelines and their maintenance, and contributed to the shared method research and business decomposition.

To evaluate this approach further, I would compare repeated-module assembly time, omitted states and the effort needed to carry a change across instances. These measures would show more concretely whether reuse helps the team.
